editorial:
Imagine living in a crowded boarding house where the tension is already high and the neighbors are annoying. You get a wild start when a mean dog breaks loose and attacks a guy who was teasing it with raw meat. After the dog is shot, you might think the danger is gone, but that is where things get weird. You follow a nervous book editor who is already on edge because everyone picks on him. Soon, he starts seeing the dead dog in his dreams, and the house becomes a nightmare as dead, chewed-up people start showing up everywhere. It feels like a bad dream that you just cannot wake up from.

The acting is solid for an indie flick, and the way the movie builds up the stress makes you feel just as anxious as the main character. While some of the special effects look a bit old, they actually add to the creepy vibe of the early eighties. If you like slow-burn horror that messes with your head, you will really dig this one.
endingExplained: Everything comes to a head when you realize the horror is happening inside the editor's mind. The dead tenants and the returning dog are symbols of his own breaking point. In the end, the line between what is real and what is a dream totally disappears. He finally snaps, and the movie closes with the realization that the mental pressure from the people around him turned his life into a living nightmare that he cannot escape.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves retro horror movies and psychological thrillers.
